summary: This is a simple Pascal program that prints the text 'Hello, world!' to the console. It's the classic first program people write when learning a new language, demonstrating the basic structure of a Pascal program with a program declaration, a begin-end block, and a single output statement.

explanations.1: This line declares that we're writing a Pascal program and gives it the name 'HelloWorld'.
explanations.2: The 'begin' keyword marks the start of the main block of code that will actually run when the program executes.
explanations.3: writeln is a built-in function that prints text to the screen and then moves to a new line; the text in single quotes is what gets printed.
explanations.4: The 'end.' keyword (with a period) marks the end of the program — the period is required syntax in Pascal to signal the program is complete.
